subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with `RequestError`, or keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: The gateway now has structured error kinds, but the ACP SDK stop-reason contract cannot encode those classes directly, so the fix requires a client-visible compatibility choice rather than a purely mechanical code change.

options.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
options.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures after avoiding SDK code conflicts, keeping reconnect behavior intentional, and requiring real ACP proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve Resolved Prompt Responses
options.body: Keep the existing resolved `PromptResponse` model and expose structured failure information through an explicitly approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Pause For Replacement
options.body: Leave this issue open for a maintainer-led or refreshed implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures after avoiding SDK code conflicts, keeping reconnect behavior intentional, and requiring real ACP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The structured error-kind classification and focused ACP tests trace to this recent area work, making this the best available owner for the contract choice.
